solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relative gets a quarter — that's a relief!

parts.note: north-east, NE, is a quarter of the compass or of a map
phew is the exclamation of someone relieved

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with relief at receiving a quarter share of an inheritance from a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A quarter' is not a fraction here but a compass quarter; 'gets' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Hastened up with speed to tell the tale

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for hastened is read from bottom to top

parts.note: hastened means ran
a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: Someone hurries up to a group, eager to recount a story quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'up' means read from bottom to top; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to give a narrative of events.

clue.text: Posse that is organised with all speed

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters being put into a new order

explanation.surface: A sheriff's posse, once properly organised, rides off at full speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges POSSE and THAT; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an adverb meaning very quickly, as fast as possible.

clue.text: Incomplete oriental holiday

indicators.note: incomplete tells us the word for oriental loses its final letter

parts.note: oriental means eastern

explanation.surface: A holiday in the Orient was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' drops the last letter N from EASTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring festival celebrating the Resurrection is a public holiday in many countries.

clue.text: Bob indicates a more direct route

explanation.surface: A bob in a signal suggests a quicker way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is a short hairstyle, literally a short cut of hair; 'indicates' only joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a haircut kept short, and a quicker path avoiding the long way round is also one.

clue.text: Cape familiar to the matador?

explanation.surface: A bullfighter's cape, a familiar sight in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Horn is the southern tip of South America; the matador sees the bull's horns all too closely. 'Cape' tempts as the matador's cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Horn is a famous headland, and the bull's pointed weapon is well known to anyone in the bullring.

clue.text: Recall soldiers and arm

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A call to bring back the troops and their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' suggests a weapon but is a body part; RE (Royal Engineers) is a standard crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind.

clue.text: Collector's piece that will be odd to us

indicators.note: the clue says this word will become the word for odd when us is added, so us comes off that longer word

parts.note: odd means curious
taken as written

explanation.surface: A collector's item that looks strange to ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'the answer will be odd with US added to it': CURIOUS minus US.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a small rare or unusual object prized by collectors.

clue.text: An outside line to ring

parts.note: reads like a telephone line for external calls, but in geometry it is a straight line touching a circle from outside

explanation.surface: A request for an outside telephone line to make a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests telephoning but is a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it.

clue.text: Check one's surrounded by others

indicators.note: surrounded by tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the rest means the others
one's is I (one) plus S, read as one is

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a person is hemmed in by other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I plus S; the pair sits inside the word for others near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an advance is to hold it back, oppose it.

clue.text: Neat island type of boat

parts.note: neat means trim, tidy
Aran is an island group off the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A tidy island has its own style of boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing vessel with three parallel hulls is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Moving sailor's call for dismissal?

explanation.surface: A sailor shouts when he is being sent away from the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry sailors gave when hauling ropes; 'giving someone the heave-ho' means sacking them.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the shanty cry as crews hauled together, and in slang to give someone this is to throw them out.

clue.text: Bad advice he obtained

indicators.note: bad advice suggests these letters are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A man got poor guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges ADVICE and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Achieved means attained or gained through effort.

clue.text: I'm taking a certain attitude for tax

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
a pose is a deliberate attitude of the body

explanation.surface: Someone adopts a particular stance on taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link joining IM and POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone's patience is to place a burden on it, as a demand is laid upon them.

clue.text: Performing with an academic chap continuously

parts.note: an actor performing is on stage
taken as written
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: Someone shares a stage with a professor who never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: A DON is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means without stopping, going on at length.

clue.text: Possibly the language of Alexander Selkirk?

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: Wonders what tongue the castaway Alexander Selkirk might have spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: Selkirk was the Scottish sailor marooned on a Pacific island, the model for Robinson Crusoe; Erse is Scottish Gaelic, so the hidden word fits the story too.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of the Scottish Highlands and Ireland.

clue.text: Preacher gives Lent a transformation

indicators.note: a transformation changes the order of the letters that precede it

explanation.surface: A preacher urges that Lent be a period of personal change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformation' rearranges the letters of GIVES LENT A.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is a person who spreads the Christian gospel through preaching.

clue.text: Simulated take-off

explanation.surface: A pretend launch of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' suggests a plane leaving the ground but here means a mimicking impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Fake leather is described as this, and a comic impersonation of someone is one.

clue.text: Solid block of cars

explanation.surface: A sturdy chunk of motor vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: A geometric solid with circular ends; car engines have a cylinder block.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry it is a three-dimensional figure with round ends, and in a motor engine it is the chamber housing a piston.

clue.text: Extremely slender, for example, that's about all

indicators.note: about indicates the abbreviation goes round the other words

parts.note: extremely means very
slender means thin

explanation.surface: A remark that being extremely slim is the be-all and end-all.
explanation.walkthrough: E and G sit around VERYTHIN; 'that's' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole lot, every single thing, is the total amount.

clue.text: Singular mistake in Latin translation

parts.note: suggests a blunder made while translating Latin, but describes the Latin singular word for one error in print

explanation.surface: A student makes a remarkable blunder translating a Latin passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' seems to mean remarkable but is the grammatical number; the plural is errata.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in writing or printing, the singular form of the Latin word.

clue.text: See you get five to one each way

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
I is the Roman numeral for one
EW is the betting abbreviation for each way

explanation.surface: A punter is told that the odds are five to one, each way.
explanation.walkthrough: Each way is a British betting term for a bet on a horse to win or be placed, written EW; the betting odds surface hides Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something is to look at or behold it.

clue.text: Tributes to the dead from the wars

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is formed out of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Memorial garlands laid for those killed in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges THE WARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreaths are circles of flowers laid at funerals and memorials.

clue.text: Leave without resources — need way to get currency

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Someone left penniless needs a means of getting some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' and 'to get' are links between definition and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone stranded is to abandon them helpless, without means.

clue.text: Getting the wind up — retreat!

explanation.surface: Someone takes fright and orders a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: To get the wind up is British slang for becoming frightened, so flinching back; there is also a hint of RE-COIL, to wind up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking back in fright is what a scared person does, and drawing back or springing back is a withdrawal.

clue.text: Length of pitch for batting after tea

indicators.note: after tells us the batting word follows the tea word

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator on how long the pitch looks for batting after the tea interval.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket pitch is 22 yards long, which is one chain, an old British unit; tea is a break in a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a surveyor's measure of 22 yards, exactly the length of a cricket pitch.

clue.text: Snake and dog in crafty contest

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
to dog someone is to follow or trace them

explanation.surface: A snake and a dog face each other in a contest of cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' means involving craft, that is boats, not cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: A race between rowing crews is a contest of craft in the boating sense.

clue.text: Rabbit's tail docked to a point

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
docked means cut short

explanation.surface: A rabbit's tail has been cut down to a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: Docking is cutting an animal's tail short, which fits the rabbit surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: A crying need for free trade cut

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose to form a new order

explanation.surface: Someone begs for a free trade cut as urgently as anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks part of the phrase free trade, but it rearranges TRADE CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping requires the small channel that carries fluid from the eye's gland.

clue.text: A trial could result in the noose

indicators.note: these words indicate the letters can be reworked into the answer

explanation.surface: A court hearing might end in a hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could result in' rearranges A TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a rope with a running loop.

clue.text: Its members are outnumbered

parts.note: describes a group smaller than the rest of the population

explanation.definitionFit: A smaller group within a larger body has fewer people than the majority.

clue.text: A Spaniard is taken for a Greek

parts.note: don is a Spanish gentleman's title

explanation.surface: A Spanish man is mistaken for a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken for' is the link; Adonis is the beautiful youth of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was a youth of classical myth loved by Aphrodite.
